program.title: MMA Beginner S&C Foundation Week 1
program.goal: Build full-body strength, trunk control, and shoulder durability while managing mild shoulder irritation from striking

athlete_analysis.profile_summary: Beginner MMA athlete, 1 session/week, 60 min available, mild shoulder irritation post-striking. Needs foundational strength and trunk stability without aggravating shoulder.
primary_constraints: Mild shoulder irritation triggered by striking—avoid overhead load and high-volume striking prep
1 session/week requires high efficiency and full-body stimulus in single session
Beginner level across all MMA domains—prioritize movement quality and pain-free execution
sport_demands: Trunk control and anti-rotation for grappling defense and striking power transfer
Shoulder stability and external rotation capacity for safe punching mechanics and armlock defense
Hip and glute strength for stance, level changes, and ground transitions
athlete_analysis.block_priority: Establish pain-free movement baseline, teach loaded hip extension and anti-rotation, build aerobic base for MMA conditioning prep. Hold striking volume until shoulder irritation resolves.

weeks.theme: Foundation strength and trunk control for MMA base

workouts.title: Full-Body Strength: Legs, Trunk, Shoulder Stability
sport_transfer: Glute and hip strength supports level changes, sprawl mechanics, and ground position stability
Anti-rotation control protects spine during grappling and transfers striking power
External rotation and scapular stability reduce shoulder injury risk during pad work and submissions
workouts.why_this_session: Build MMA-ready hip and trunk strength without loading irritated shoulder; establishes pain-free baseline for rapid progression.

warmup.name: Dead Bug
warmup.purpose: Activate core and teach trunk neutrality without spinal load

warmup.name: Glute Bridge
warmup.purpose: Activate glutes and cue hip extension pattern without loading

warmup.name: Side-Lying Dumbbell External Rotation
warmup.purpose: Prepare rotator cuff and scapular stability with light load
warmup.load_guidance: Light dumbbell, 2–5 kg, focus on control not load

main_work.name: Barbell Glute Bridge
main_work.purpose: Build loaded hip extension strength for grappling position stability and power
main_work.load_guidance: Start light (bar + 10 kg per side); progress by 2–5 kg per week if pain-free

main_work.name: Dumbbell Split Squat
main_work.purpose: Build single-leg strength and hip control for unilateral stability during striking and level changes
main_work.load_guidance: Dumbbells 8–12 kg per hand; adjust for balanced front-leg loading

main_work.name: Half-Kneeling Landmine Press
main_work.purpose: Train horizontal pressing and anti-rotation trunk control without high shoulder load
main_work.load_guidance: Start 10 kg per side; prioritize pelvis/rib alignment over load

main_work.name: Dumbbell Floor Press
main_work.purpose: Build pressing strength with reduced shoulder range and joint protection
main_work.load_guidance: Dumbbells 8–12 kg per hand; floor contact limits depth and reduces irritation risk

cooldown.name: Glute Bridge Hold
cooldown.purpose: Release and lengthen hip flexors post-session

cooldown.name: Dead Bug
cooldown.purpose: Restore trunk control and centering post-session

injury_modifications: If shoulder irritation increases during press work, reduce pressing volume to 2 sets and lower load by 20–30%; defer dumbbell floor press to week 2
If kneeling position causes knee discomfort, place thin pad under knee and reduce depth; or substitute Leg Press for Split Squat
If low-back rounding appears on glute bridge, reduce load and cue posterior pelvic tilt before each rep

weeks.progression_rule: Establish baseline pain-free movement with moderate loads. Progress week 2 to heavier legs, more demanding anti-rotation if shoulder remains irritation-free.

program.nutrition_focus: Moderate protein intake (1.6–2.0 g/kg) to support single-session recovery; ensure adequate carbs around training for energy and glute bridge loading; hydrate consistently given 7h sleep baseline.
recovery_focus: Sleep consistency: maintain 7h nightly to support strength adaptation and shoulder irritation healing
Post-session low-intensity mobility: 5–10 min easy movement to reduce stiffness without adding fatigue
Shoulder irritation monitoring: track pain during and 24h after session; if worsening, defer pressing and add more external rotation prep week 2
safety_notes: Do not perform maximal striking or heavy bag work until shoulder irritation fully resolves; this week focuses on strength only
Maintain upright torso and stacked ribs/pelvis during landmine press to protect lumbar spine under load
If any neck, rib, or knee symptoms appear, reset with tap/verbal signal immediately and notify coach before resuming
Beginners should prioritize movement quality (hip extension depth, trunk stiffness, scapular position) over load progression in week 1
assumptions: Athlete has access to barbell, dumbbells, bench, and landmine; if not, substitute Leg Press for Glute Bridge and Machine-based alternatives for free-weight exercises
Mild shoulder irritation is mechanical and pain-free at current rest levels; assumes no labral pathology or nerve involvement
Athlete can safely enter half-kneeling position without pain and understands tap/reset protocol for partner work prep
1 session/week is temporary baseline; expect progression to 2–3 sessions/week as MMA skill and recovery capacity grow

workout_titles: Full-Body Strength: Legs, Trunk, Shoulder Stability
